content.title: About
content.content: Black beans and brown rice are a combination of plant protein, complex carbohydrates, and fiber. Beans are rich in protein, iron, and antioxidants, while brown rice retains the bran and germ, making it more nutritious than white rice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black beans are often called "young beans" and are a staple in Latin American cuisine.
Brown rice is a whole grain that keeps the bran, germ, and endosperm intact.
Together, beans and rice provide a complete set of essential amino acids, similar to animal protein.
Black beans contain anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants that give them their dark color.
When stored properly, brown rice can stay fresh for up to 6 months in a cool, dry place.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Black beans provide about 8 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Both foods supply soluble and insoluble fiber, promoting healthy digestion and blood‑sugar control.

items.title: Source of iron and magnesium
items.content: Black beans are a good source of iron, while brown rice supplies magnesium, important for nerve and muscle function.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Fiber and antioxidants help lower cholesterol and protect blood vessels from oxidative stress.

items.title: Steady energy source
items.content: Complex carbs in brown rice release glucose slowly, providing lasting satiety.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption if consumed in excess.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Beans can cause gastrointestinal discomfort in sensitive people; soaking and thorough cooking help.

items.title: Potential gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: People with celiac disease should ensure the rice is not contaminated with gluten during processing.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook beans and rice together as a side dish, in salads, soups, or as a vegetarian pilaf. Soak beans 8–12 hours, then boil until tender. Cook brown rice 40–45 minutes in a 1:2.5 rice‑to‑water ratio. Season with herbs, vegetables, and olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to a year. Keep brown rice in a tightly sealed container in the refrigerator or a dark, cool pantry to prevent the oils from becoming rancid.
